title: NeuraLUT-Assemble: Hardware-Aware Assembling of Sub-Neural Networks for Efficient LUT Inference
problem: Existing LUT-based neural network designs suffer from accuracy degradation because the fan-in required by neurons is limited by the exponential scaling of LUT resources with input width, forcing reliance on extremely sparse models that limit connectivity.
motivation: LUT-based neural networks on FPGAs promise ultra-low latency and reduced resource utilization for edge computing and emerging AI applications in fields like particle physics.
method: NeuraLUT-Assemble overcomes the fan-in limitation—the constraint that lookup tables can't efficiently handle many inputs—by combining multiple smaller lookup tables into each neuron. It uses mixed-precision quantization, representing some values with fewer bits than others, to keep the total hardware resources manageable while increasing connectivity. Skip-connections allow gradient signals to flow backward across the network during training, which improves learning. The result is competitive accuracy with traditional dense neural networks while fitting within hardware constraints.
key_novelty: Assembling neurons from smaller lookup tables with mixed-precision quantization (representing different values with different bit-widths) to overcome the fan-in limit—the maximum number of inputs a lookup table can handle.
contributions: Mixed-precision quantization framework for LUT-based neural networks
Novel neuron assembly technique combining smaller LUTs into larger functional units
Skip-connections across LUT structures for improved gradient flow
Closes accuracy gap between LUT-based methods and fully-connected MLPs
Achieves up to 8.42x reduction in area-delay product over state-of-the-art

metrics.accuracy: Competitive with MLP-based models on network intrusion detection, digit classification, and jet classification

limitations: Scalability to larger networks and comparison with other edge-deployed neural network approaches not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware-aware LUT assembly for efficient edge neural inference
